_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 5: Prohibited AI Practices
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim standard developed by ComplianceLint. Article 5 prohibitions are directly applicable since 2025-02-02 (points (ba) and (bb), added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, from 2026-12-02) and do not require harmonized standards for interpretation. This document restates the prohibitions with operational detail for compliance checking. It is NOT legal advice.
basis: EU AI Act Article 5 (official text, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)

Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus), Article 1 point (7): inserts Art. 5(1)(ba), (bb), (1a) and (1b); applicable from 2026-12-02 per Art. 113, third paragraph, point (a), as amended (consolidated text CELEX 02024R1689-20260727)
EU AI Act Annex II (list of criminal offences for Art. 5(1)(h) exception)
EU AI Act Article 99(3) (penalties for Art. 5 violations)
AI Office guidelines on prohibited practices (when available)
European Data Protection Board guidelines on biometric data processing
Fundamental Rights Agency analysis of AI Act prohibitions
_metadata.awaiting_standard: No harmonized standard required — prohibitions are directly applicable. AI Office guidelines may provide interpretive clarity.

prohibited_practices.title: Subliminal / Manipulative / Deceptive Techniques
prohibited_practices.prohibition: AI systems that deploy subliminal techniques beyond a person's consciousness, or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective or effect of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or group by appreciably impairing their ability to make an informed decision, thereby causing them to take a decision that they would not otherwise have taken, in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person, another person or a group of persons significant harm.
scope: Subliminal stimuli (visual, auditory, or other sensory signals below conscious perception threshold)
Deceptive AI-driven interfaces designed to distort decision-making (dark patterns with AI component)
AI systems that manipulate information presentation to exploit cognitive biases causing significant harm
not_in_scope: Standard recommendation algorithms (unless causing significant harm through manipulation)
AI-generated marketing content (unless using subliminal techniques)
Persuasive design without subliminal or deceptive component
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Code referencing subliminal messaging or stimulus injection
Dark pattern implementations with AI-driven personalization
A/B testing frameworks that optimize for behavioural manipulation

prohibited_practices.title: Exploitation of Vulnerabilities of Specific Groups
prohibited_practices.prohibition: AI systems that exploit any of the vulnerabilities of a person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability, or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a member of that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm.
scope: AI targeting children with manipulative content
AI exploiting elderly persons' reduced digital literacy
AI exploiting disability-related vulnerabilities (cognitive, physical, sensory)
AI exploiting vulnerability due to a specific social or economic situation (Recital 29 examples: persons living in extreme poverty, ethnic or religious minorities)
not_in_scope: AI accessibility tools designed to help vulnerable groups
AI systems providing age-appropriate content filtering
AI systems that account for vulnerability to REDUCE harm
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Code that segments users by age/disability and applies different manipulation strategies
Targeting logic specifically for vulnerable demographics
Exploitation of inferred vulnerability status for commercial advantage

prohibited_practices.title: Non-Consensual Intimate Material (Art. 5(1)(ba))
prohibited_practices.prohibition: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts, or of an identifiable natural person engaged in sexually explicit activities, without that person's freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation. Placing on the market / putting into service is prohibited only where that generation or manipulation is the intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome (without significant technical modification) of a system that lacks reasonable and adequate safeguards to reliably prevent it and to correct observed or reported misuse (Art. 5(1a)(a)); use is prohibited where the deployer uses the system for that purpose (Art. 5(1a)(b)).
scope: AI systems intended to generate or manipulate realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts, or of an identifiable natural person engaged in sexually explicit activities, without that person's freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent (for example 'nudification' applications, Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 11)

Other AI systems, including general-purpose image, video, audio or face-swap/editing systems, where the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make such generation or manipulation a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without requiring significant technical modification, and the system does not have reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards that reliably prevent that generation or manipulation, taking into account reasonably foreseeable misuse, and correct observed or reported misuse (Art. 5(1a)(a)(ii))

Deployers using any AI system for the purpose of generating or manipulating such material, including misuse of systems that lack adequate preventive measures, circumvention of preventive measures, and use of lawful systems not intended for such material (Art. 5(1a)(b); Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)
not_in_scope: Generation or manipulation with the depicted person's freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation
Developing the technical capabilities of AI systems to generate or manipulate images, videos, audio or similar material, as such (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)

Cartoonish or physically impossible depictions of a person's body: 'realistic' refers to the depiction of the person's face, voice or body in a credible real-life manner (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)

Nude material that does not depict identifiable natural persons, realistic partially nude depictions where intimate parts are not revealed and sexually explicit activities are not depicted, and non-realistic artistic nude works (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12); Art. 5(1)(bb) may still apply where the material falls within Directive 2011/93/EU

Generative applications where intimate parts are not exposed or, if exposed, exposure is subject to the depicted person's freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent, for example try-on applications and medical applications such as medical anatomical simulations and mammograms (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)

Exceptional use, in accordance with fundamental rights law, data protection law and applicable medical law, of AI systems generating or manipulating nude depictions of an identifiable person's intimate parts for medical diagnosis and treatment by medical professionals where the person concerned is incapable of consent, for instance in an emergency (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)

Use limb: use for lawful purposes, such as generating or manipulating other material, even where the system lacks the safeguards the provider should have put in place; accidental generation or manipulation (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)

Manipulation that neither increases the exposure of any depicted intimate parts nor alters the nature of any depicted sexually explicit activities (Art. 5(1b)), for instance changing the background, adding a text heading or enhancing the contrast or the brightness of existing material (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12)
prohibited_practices.exceptions: Consent of the depicted person that is freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit, for that generation or manipulation — all five qualities are required. Art. 5(1)(ba) does not specify who must collect, verify or document the consent; for AI systems intended to generate or manipulate such material, the measures and other safeguards should include appropriate means for the distribution of the AI system aimed at enabling the reliable collection and demonstration of the depicted person's consent, in compliance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12).
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Image / video / audio generation (diffusion, GAN, voice cloning) or face-swap / inpainting pipelines that accept a real person's photo, video or voice as input

Generation endpoints without the kinds of preventive measures listed in Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 12: data cleaning, refusal training, safe prompt design and output controls, runtime prompt guardrails, content classification and filtering, usage restrictions, abuse detection, notice and action
No abuse-reporting, takedown or misuse-correction workflow for generated content
Systems intended to produce intimate material without a mechanism to collect and demonstrate the depicted person's consent
Product copy, prompts, model names or features referencing undressing, nudify or deepnude

prohibited_practices.title: Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)
prohibited_practices.prohibition: The placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates material or performance within the meaning of Article 2, points (c) and (e), of Directive 2011/93/EU, except where a 'without right' defence applies under national law. Placing on the market / putting into service is prohibited only where that generation or manipulation is the intended purpose, or a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome (without significant technical modification) of a system that lacks reasonable and adequate safeguards to reliably prevent it and to correct observed or reported misuse (Art. 5(1a)(a)); use is prohibited where the deployer uses the system for that purpose (Art. 5(1a)(b)).
scope: AI systems whose intended purpose is to generate or manipulate material or performance within Directive 2011/93/EU Art. 2(c) or (e)

Other AI systems, including general-purpose systems for generating or manipulating visual material or live performances, where the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make generation or manipulation of material or performance within Directive 2011/93/EU Art. 2(c) or (e) a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without requiring significant technical modification, and the system does not have reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and other safeguards that reliably prevent it, taking into account reasonably foreseeable misuse, and correct observed or reported misuse (Art. 5(1a)(a)(ii))
Deployers using any AI system for the purpose of generating or manipulating such material or performance (Art. 5(1a)(b))
not_in_scope: Cases where a 'without right' defence applies under the national law of the Member State concerned (Art. 5(1)(bb))

Where such a defence applies: activities carried out under domestic legal powers, such as the legitimate generation or manipulation of such material by the authorities in order to conduct criminal proceedings or to prevent, detect or investigate crime, and the legitimate use of the AI system for red-teaming and evaluation activities to assess the system's compliance with this prohibition (Reg (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 13)
prohibited_practices.exceptions: 'Without right' defence under national law. The material scope is defined by Directive 2011/93/EU Art. 2(c) and (e); ComplianceLint cites, and does not paraphrase, that Directive.
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Image or video generation or editing pipelines without sexual-content and minor-detection output classifiers
No hash-matching or known-CSAM detection on inputs or outputs where users can upload or generate imagery
No abuse-reporting, takedown or misuse-correction workflow for generated content
Fine-tuning or LoRA datasets / model cards without documented exclusion of sexual content involving minors

prohibited_practices.title: Social Scoring
prohibited_practices.prohibition: AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred, or predicted personal or personality characteristics, with the social score leading to either or both: (i) detrimental or unfavourable treatment in social contexts unrelated to the contexts where the data was originally generated or collected; (ii) detrimental or unfavourable treatment that is unjustified or disproportionate to their social behaviour or its gravity.
scope: Systems that aggregate social behaviour data into a 'score' affecting access to services
Systems that use personal characteristics to create trustworthiness ratings with real-world consequences
Cross-context data aggregation leading to discriminatory treatment (e.g., social media behaviour affecting credit)
not_in_scope: Credit scoring based solely on financial behaviour (regulated under separate financial law)
Reputation systems limited to a single service context (e.g., seller ratings on a marketplace)
Fraud detection scoring within the same service context
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Social scoring variables or functions
Cross-context person rating/ranking systems
Trustworthiness score computation from social behaviour data
Behaviour aggregation across multiple unrelated domains

prohibited_practices.title: Criminal Offence Risk Assessment Based Solely on Profiling
prohibited_practices.prohibition: AI systems that make risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics. This prohibition does not apply to AI systems used to support the human assessment of the involvement of a person in a criminal activity, which is already based on objective, verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity.
scope: Predictive policing systems that profile individuals (not locations) for criminal risk
Recidivism prediction based solely on personality/demographic profiling
Pre-crime assessment tools based on personal characteristics without factual criminal evidence
not_in_scope: AI augmenting human assessment based on objective criminal evidence
Crime hotspot prediction (location-based, not person-based)
Fraud detection based on transactional patterns (not personality profiling)
prohibited_practices.exceptions: AI supporting human assessment based on objective, verifiable facts directly linked to criminal activity
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Criminal risk scoring functions
Recidivism prediction models
Person-level crime risk profiling (distinct from location-based crime prediction)

prohibited_practices.title: Untargeted Facial Image Scraping
prohibited_practices.prohibition: AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage.
scope: Scraping facial images from social media, websites, or public internet sources
Collecting facial images from CCTV systems without targeted, lawful basis
Building or expanding facial recognition training datasets through bulk untargeted collection
not_in_scope: Facial recognition databases built from consented, targeted data collection
Facial recognition using images from lawful, targeted investigations (law enforcement with proper authorization)
Research on publicly available facial recognition benchmark datasets (context-dependent)
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Web scraping combined with face detection/extraction
CCTV feed processing with face extraction pipelines
Bulk image download scripts combined with facial recognition libraries
Face database building or expansion code

prohibited_practices.title: Emotion Recognition in Workplace and Education
prohibited_practices.prohibition: AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where the AI system is intended to be put into service or placed on the market for medical or safety reasons.
scope: Employee engagement/mood detection AI in workplace settings
Student attention/emotion monitoring in educational institutions
AI-driven interview emotion analysis for hiring decisions
Workplace productivity monitoring via emotion inference
not_in_scope: Emotion recognition for medical/therapeutic purposes (e.g., mental health monitoring with consent)

Detection of physical states such as fatigue or pain (e.g., fatigue detection for professional pilots or drivers) — not emotion recognition at all (Recital 18), so outside the prohibition rather than within the safety exception
Systems labelled as attention or engagement monitoring that do not infer emotions (Art. 3(39): identifying or inferring emotions or intentions on the basis of biometric data)
Emotion recognition in entertainment, gaming, or voluntary consumer applications
Emotion recognition in customer service (outside workplace/education context)
prohibited_practices.exceptions: Use intended to be put in place or into the market for medical reasons (Recital 44 example: systems intended for therapeutical use) or for safety reasons. Art. 5(1)(f) states no separate documentation or other formal condition for these exceptions.
exception_requirements: Good practice, NOT a statutory condition of Art. 5(1)(f): record the medical or safety purpose for which the system is intended, so the exception can be evidenced
Good practice, NOT a statutory condition of Art. 5(1)(f): confirm that emotion inference is needed for that medical or safety purpose
Other law continues to apply (e.g., GDPR for the biometric data processed)
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Emotion/sentiment detection libraries in workplace/education context
Facial expression analysis in employee/student monitoring systems
Voice emotion analysis in workplace communication tools
Engagement/attention scoring in education platforms

prohibited_practices.title: Biometric Categorization Inferring Sensitive Attributes
prohibited_practices.prohibition: Biometric categorization systems that categorize individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation. This prohibition does not apply to any labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, such as images, based on biometric data or categorizing of biometric data in the area of law enforcement.
scope: AI that analyses facial features, voice, gait, or other biometric data to infer race or ethnicity
AI that infers political opinions from biometric data
AI that infers religious beliefs from biometric data (e.g., facial hair, clothing detection as proxy)
AI that infers sexual orientation from biometric data
AI that infers trade union membership from biometric data
not_in_scope: Biometric data processing that does not attempt to infer the listed sensitive attributes
Lawful labelling/filtering of biometric datasets (e.g., annotating training data with consent)
Law enforcement categorization of biometric data under applicable legal basis
Gender detection for accessibility purposes (context-dependent, seek legal advice)
prohibited_practices.exceptions: Lawful labelling or filtering of biometric datasets acquired in line with EU or national law; categorization of biometric data in law enforcement
prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Race/ethnicity classification from facial images
Political opinion inference from biometric data
Sexual orientation prediction from biometric data
Religion inference from physical appearance analysis

prohibited_practices.title: Real-Time Remote Biometric Identification in Public Spaces
prohibited_practices.prohibition: The use of 'real-time' remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement, unless and in as far as such use is strictly necessary for one of the listed objectives.
scope: Live facial recognition cameras in public spaces (streets, parks, transport hubs)
Real-time gait recognition in publicly accessible areas
Live voice identification in public spaces
Any real-time biometric matching against watchlists in public areas
not_in_scope: Post-remote (non-real-time) biometric identification — not prohibited by Art. 5(1)(h); high-risk under Art. 6(2) and Annex III point 1(a), in so far as its use is permitted under relevant Union or national law
Biometric verification (1:1 matching, e.g., unlocking a phone)

Biometric identification in places NOT accessible to an undetermined number of natural persons (e.g., areas restricted to authorised staff). Private ownership or conditions for access do not by themselves take a place outside 'publicly accessible space' (Art. 3(44))
Non-law-enforcement real-time biometric identification (high-risk under Art. 6(2) and Annex III point 1(a), not banned by Art. 5(1)(h))

exceptions.description: Three strictly limited exceptions for law enforcement, each requiring prior authorisation by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding (Art. 5(3)); in a duly justified situation of urgency, use may start without authorisation provided it is requested without undue delay, at the latest within 24 hours
exceptions.exception_i: Targeted search for specific victims of abduction, trafficking, sexual exploitation, or search for missing persons
exceptions.exception_ii: Prevention of a specific, substantial, and imminent threat to the life or physical safety of natural persons, or a genuine and present or foreseeable threat of a terrorist attack
exceptions.exception_iii: Localization or identification of a person suspected of having committed a criminal offence punishable by a custodial sentence of at least 4 years, for offences listed in Annex II
conditions: Must be strictly necessary for the stated objective

Only to confirm the identity of the specifically targeted individual, taking into account the seriousness, probability and scale of the harm if not used and of the consequences for the rights and freedoms of all persons concerned (Art. 5(2))

Prior authorisation by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding; in urgency, request without undue delay, at the latest within 24 hours; if rejected, stop immediately and delete all data, results and outputs (Art. 5(3))
Necessary and proportionate safeguards and conditions in accordance with the national law authorising the use, in particular temporal, geographic and personal limitations (Art. 5(2))
Completed fundamental rights impact assessment (Art. 27) before authorisation
Registration in the EU database (Art. 49); in duly justified urgency, use may start before registration provided registration is completed without undue delay
Each use notified to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority (Art. 5(4))
National law may further restrict or prohibit these exceptions

prohibited_practices.penalty: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(3)); for SMEs, including start-ups, Art. 99(6) applies the lower cap.
heuristic_indicators: Real-time facial recognition pipeline with camera/stream input
Live biometric matching against watchlists or databases
Surveillance system integration with biometric identification
Public space deployment configuration for biometric systems

compliance_assessment.methodology: For each prohibited practice, determine: (1) Does the AI system fall within the practice's scope? (2) If yes, does any exception apply? (3) If an exception applies, are all conditions met?
compliance_assessment.clean_scan_note: A clean automated scan (no heuristic flags) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for Art. 5 compliance. Automated tools cannot assess deployment context, intent, or real-world effect.
compliance_assessment.documentation_requirement: All Art. 5 compliance assessments should be documented in writing, including the assessment date, assessor, methodology, and conclusions for each prohibited practice.

scoring.compliant: No heuristic indicators found AND documented human review confirms no prohibited practices
scoring.unable_to_determine: Heuristic indicators found — human review required to determine compliance
scoring.non_compliant: Human review confirms a prohibited practice is implemented without valid exception
